## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `54666faed39647037682b61f6b6a510b044e6c64`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md + packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`delete_record` registration, `recordDeleteConfirmationRefusal`, `codedErrorResult`, `run_action` / `resume_run` descriptions), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_CODE` / `_STATUS`, `actionConfirmationRefusal`), packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts (`AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER`), packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts (the served MCP skill's `delete_record` line), scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs (the `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` row), .changeset/30863-skills-ai-delete-record-confirm.md, packages/skills/package.json, skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json, and the rest of `skills/**` (swept for `delete_record` teaching)

### ① Derived judgments

The net diff against `main` (merge base `8ae0ab9b0`, which is `origin/main` itself) is two files. One row of `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` is replaced in place (L202), and one changeset is added. No schema, export, metadata key, accept-set or runtime behaviour changes. The only published surface that moves is the `@objectstack/skills` catalog text.

- **Teaching surface (L202): right.** The tools-table row for `create_record` / `update_record` / `delete_record` used to say only "`delete_record` is annotated destructive". It now says that `delete_record` is refused with `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (428) unless it sends `confirm: true`, and that the agent asks the human first and then retries. The skill now agrees with the accept-set the server has had since PR #30861 (`c77dd17f26`). Before this change, an agent that followed the row sent no `confirm` and was refused.
- **Accept-set implied: none new.** The row introduces no argument, code or value that `main` lacks. `confirm` is `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts:242`). It is declared on the `delete_record` input schema as an optional boolean (`mcp-http-tools.ts:1593`). The handler gate admits only the boolean `true` (`mcp-http-tools.ts:564`).
- **Eval surface: unchanged, and right to stay unchanged.** `skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json` is this skill's only eval file. No case in it mentions `delete_record`, `confirm`, `destructive` or MCP write tools; its cases grade `query_records` / `get_record` / action tools in `defineSkill` / `defineAgent` authoring. So no stale eval remains in this skill.
- **Sweep of the rest of `skills/**`: clean.** The remaining `delete_record` mentions are the flow node type, not the MCP tool: `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` L89 and L203, and `skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md` L193. No file outside this row teaches the MCP `delete_record` call, so nothing sends it without `confirm`.

### ② Semver level

The changeset holds `'@objectstack/skills': patch`, `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR body carries the same two declaration lines. This matches what the diff publishes.

- `@objectstack/skills` (`packages/skills/package.json`) is the package that ships the `skills/**` tree as its `dist` catalog. The edited row is the only published byte that changes.
- `Clause-②: no` is right: no spec or accept-set changes, so there is neither a widening nor a narrowing.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, value, metadata type, meaning or default that an author can write changes.
- `patch` is the level that `none` takes. No `skip-changeset` is used, which is correct because the diff publishes text from a released package.
- No other package bundles this file. `packages/spec/scripts/check-skill-examples.ts` reads `skills/**` but is a check script, not a published artifact.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR body: contract-review tier waived for the dev, under the maintainer's standing order (2026-11-03).** Answered: this record is the contract-tier review the PR body says the dispatching seat owes.
- **PR body: "需要你做的:无".** No open question is put to the maintainer, and none remains open for this record.
- **PR body: 45 local gates, exit 0.** Not relied on; this record reads the head's check-runs instead. At 17:11Z, 38 check-runs were on the head. 29 had finished: 18 success and 11 skipped, with no failure. 9 were still in progress: `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)` and `Live E2E UI`. The skill gates (token ratchet, `check:skill-docs`, identifier liveness and frame sync) ride in the Lint jobs that are still running, so their verdicts are not in yet. Among those already green: `Check Changeset`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `PR-body guards`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Check PR Size`. Landing still waits for the in-progress runs.
- **Follow-up, escalated and outside this card's declared surface (L202 only): the adjacent `list_actions`, `run_action` row (L203).** It does not teach `run_action`'s own `confirm: true` for an action whose author set `ai.requiresConfirmation`. The rest of SKILL.md names `ai.requiresConfirmation` only as an author-side gate (L154, L317) and never names the caller's `confirm` member. Now that L202 teaches the member for `delete_record`, an agent may read its absence on L203 as "`run_action` never needs it". The server's own `run_action` description does teach it, so this is a gap in the skill, not a refusal the skill causes. It is a candidate for a separate card. It does not block this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

Each claim in the new row was checked against the code on `main`.

- **The code is `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`: holds.** `recordDeleteConfirmationRefusal` (`mcp-http-tools.ts:558-579`) returns `code: ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, typed as the registered `ErrorCode`. This is the same literal as the runtime's `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_CODE` (`action-execution.ts:2869`), which `run_action`'s door answers with.
- **428 on the MCP path: holds as written, no finding.** On MCP there is no HTTP 428 at the transport. The handler returns `codedErrorResult`, which is a tool error (`isError: true`) whose text is the JSON `{ error: { code, message, status, details } }`, and the JSON-RPC exchange itself succeeds. But `status` in that envelope is `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_HTTP_STATUS = 428` (`mcp-http-tools.ts:526`), mirrored from the runtime's `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_STATUS = 428` (`action-execution.ts:2877`), so the agent does see `"status":428` in the tool result it reads. "(428)" after the code is also the house shorthand for this refusal (`http-dispatcher.ts:1376` writes "`ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, 428"). The row puts the code first, and the code is what an agent branches on. So the parenthetical is accurate and not misleading.
- **The argument is exactly `confirm` and the value exactly `true`: holds.** The schema key is `[AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER]` = `'confirm'`, `z.boolean().optional()`, and the gate tests `=== true`. Absent or `false` gets the coded refusal. The input is strict (`strictToolInput`), so a string `"true"` fails schema validation as an input error, which is also a refusal with nothing deleted. The row's literal `confirm: true` is therefore the only call that passes, which is exactly what it teaches.
- **"ask the human first, then retry": holds.** It is verbatim from the server's own `delete_record` description (`mcp-http-tools.ts:1581-1582`: "A call is REFUSED unless it also sends confirm: true — ask the human first, then retry"). It is also verbatim from the server's `run_action` description (L1696-1697), which is the wording rule the card asks for. The refusal message says the same thing in its own words ("confirm with the human in the loop, then retry this call with 'confirm': true"). The served MCP skill text (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts:288-291`) teaches the same call, so the two skill surfaces agree.
- **Scope of the claim: holds.** The gate runs before the bridge for every object (`mcp-http-tools.ts:1610`, "no object is exempt"). The only earlier refusal is the system-object `guard`, which the row does not contradict. `create_record` / `update_record` stay ungated, as the row implies by naming only `delete_record`. The row drops the words "annotated destructive", but `destructiveHint: true` still stands on the tool and the new sentence subsumes it for an agent, so no fact the agent needs is lost.
- **Token and line budget: holds.** The ratchet counts `ceil(utf8 bytes / 4)` after excluding the release-stamp line (`  version: "18.3.0"` plus newline, 20 bytes).
  - Head blob: 22272 bytes, 20 stamp bytes excluded, which is 5563 tokens.
  - `main` blob: 22176 bytes, 20 stamp bytes excluded, which is 5539 tokens.
  - Row ceiling: 6801 (`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs:369`, unchanged by this PR). Headroom is 1238.
  - This matches the PR body's 5539 → 5563 / 6801 / 1238 exactly. The raw count without the exclusion is 5544 → 5568.
  - Lines: 421 → 421, so the net line change in `skills/**` is 0.

No must-fix and no should-fix. The new row holds against `main`'s code and against the card's expected behaviour.
